# Population vocabulary

Definitions of the shared terms used by the population reference. A type-chain name
describes inheritance; an applied API name describes additional behavior on a prim.

## USD

Universal Scene Description (OpenUSD): a scene-description system that composes layers into a hierarchy of named scene elements (prims), with typed properties and relationships. In this workflow, ovstage population reads USD; the ovphysx simulation library does not embed OpenUSD.

## ovstage

The column-oriented scene store used by the runtime. A Stage holds named prims and their attribute columns; population writes values, and consumers read snapshots at sealed ordinals (ordered versions of the Stage).

## prim

A named scene element at a unique absolute path, such as /World/Box. Its type, applied API schemas, properties and relationships describe that element. Parent paths define the scene hierarchy.

## ovphysx

The standalone C library and Python package that attaches an ovstage Stage to the PhysX runtime, advances the simulation and exchanges state through read/write sessions.

## Xformable

The USD base schema for prims that can carry spatial transforms. Their local transform normally composes with ancestor transforms; resetXformStack stops that inheritance. A type-chain entry expresses schema inheritance, not a separately authored attribute.

## PhysX

NVIDIA's physics simulation engine. The runtime creates PhysX actors, shapes, joints and scenes from populated scene data; the SDK classes named Px... describe those engine objects.

## Typed

The USD base schema for prims with a registered concrete type name. A type chain lists the schema ancestors of that concrete type; it is distinct from the list of applied API schemas.

## Gprim

The USD geometric-primitive base schema, inherited by geometric types such as meshes, cubes and spheres. Geometry alone does not make a collider; a shape-consuming physics API must also apply.

## Imageable

The USD base schema for scene elements that can participate in rendering, including properties such as visibility and purpose. Being imageable does not by itself make a prim part of the physics simulation.

## compiled stage cache

The optional stored representation of a supported attachment's parsed physics data. A matching cache identity permits restoring cached data instead of repeating supported parsing and geometry cooking (conversion to simulation shapes); unsupported components bypass that cache. This is separate from the live simulation state.

## Mesh

A USD geometric type described by vertex positions and indexed polygon faces. Physics collision APIs select how that surface is cooked into a simulation shape.

## IsaacLab

Isaac Lab, NVIDIA's robot-learning framework, which uses batched simulation environments for tasks such as reinforcement learning. Its schema conventions can add metadata to otherwise ordinary USD/PhysX scenes.

## Boundable

The USD base schema for imageable geometry with a spatial extent (a bounding region). It is a type ancestor used by population when deciding which geometric relationship targets need rows.

## PhysicsJoint

The USD base physics-joint type. It relates body0 and body1 through their local joint frames; concrete joint types add their own constrained or free motion rules.

## UsdLux

The OpenUSD schema family for lights and their shared lighting properties. Light types can appear in populated data without creating a physics object.

## Material

A USD material prim: a named container that can be bound to geometry. Applied physics material APIs supply simulation properties such as friction; a Material type alone does not supply those values.

## PxD6Joint

The PhysX SDK joint with six configurable degrees of freedom: three translations and three rotations between two actor frames. Each axis can be locked, limited or free, subject to the joint's configuration.

## BoundableLightBase

The USD light base schema for light types with a finite spatial extent. It is part of their type ancestry; its presence alone does not create a physics shape.

## PxDistanceJoint

The PhysX SDK joint that constrains the distance between two actor-frame points, with optional minimum/maximum distance and spring behavior.

## PointBased

The USD base schema for geometry whose shape is described by point positions, such as a mesh or a point cloud. Concrete types define how the points form geometry.

## NonboundableLightBase

The USD light base schema for light types that do not describe a finite geometric extent. It is type ancestry used for classification, not an applied physics API.

## token id

An integer produced by interning a string (registering or looking it up) in a Stage's token dictionary. It denotes that exact string in that dictionary. Type/schema tokens are not interchangeable with prim path ids, and raw ids must not be transferred between unrelated dictionaries.

## Fabric

NVIDIA's column-oriented scene-data infrastructure. In this reference, Fabric-named transform columns identify stored scene transforms; their names and precedence are part of the population contract.

## PointInstancer

The USD type that places many instances of prototype geometry using arrays of prototype indices, positions, orientations and scales. An instance's slot in those arrays is distinct from the prototype prim's path.

## SI

The International System of Units. The relevant base units here are meters for length, kilograms for mass and seconds for time; stage-unit metadata states the conversion from authored scene length and mass units.
